name: Battery

claims.claim_text: Lithium-ion cells are made in two upper-voltage variants: a coke-anode cell that terminates at 4.1 volts and the more common graphite-anode cell that terminates at 4.2 volts, and roughly ninety percent of available charger parts are built for the 4.2-volt figure.
claims.quote_verbatim: it was a 4.1 volt battery, which uses a Coke anode, it's called, as opposed to a graphite anode, which is 4.2 volts
claims.episode_title: Autorouter, Datasheets & Obscure Chips - Cloddish Collegiate Conversations

claims.claim_text: Selecting a lithium charger IC begins with a parametric search on termination voltage, which distributors expose as a sortable characteristic, but the minimum charge current a part can deliver is not a parametric field and has to be read out of each candidate data sheet by hand.
claims.quote_verbatim: But then when you've got to go through and look at each individual data sheet to see if it can do the minimum current you require
claims.episode_title: Autorouter, Datasheets & Obscure Chips - Cloddish Collegiate Conversations

claims.claim_text: A primary cell powering a microamp-class part can have a shelf life on the order of eight years, which becomes the limit on the design rather than the load current.
claims.quote_verbatim: That's 2,900 days or 365 equals eight years. Eight years is basically the shelf life of the battery.
claims.episode_title: Analog Devices, Design Spark - Unusual Usenet Usurpation

claims.claim_text: Usable capacity is set by the load's minimum operating voltage, not by the cell's rating: a three-volt cell feeding a part that stops working at 2.5 volts leaves most of the stored energy unreachable, so an eight-year nominal life collapses to months unless a DC-DC converter holds the rail constant as the cell falls.
claims.quote_verbatim: unless you had a DC to DC converter in there to keep a constant voltage, you wouldn't use up all the usable capacity in the battery because its lowest voltage is 2.5 volts
claims.episode_title: Chairs, Sparks and Devices - Optional Olent Obreption

claims.claim_text: Batteries perform poorly at low temperature, so an instrument specified to operate down to freezing or below can fail on its power source rather than its circuitry; alkaline cells in particular lose usable output near zero degrees Celsius.
claims.quote_verbatim: batteries are very poor performers down at low temperatures
claims.episode_title: Tektronix, ChipReport.tv, & the Signal Path - Temperative Tegmen Temperature

claims.claim_text: Lithium recovery from cell recycling reaches about ninety-five percent, so the mined material is largely retained across a cell's disposal cycle.
claims.quote_verbatim: we can get right at 95% of the lithium recovered from the recycling
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: An electric-vehicle pack is treated as having reached the end of its first life when it has lost twenty percent of its capacity; whether that takes five, eight or ten years depends on cell stress, temperature and how conservatively the pack is managed.
claims.quote_verbatim: One lifetime is the active use of the cell, and the 80% level is considered the first lifetime
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: Hybrid-vehicle manufacturers keep the pack centred on fifty percent state of charge and swing only plus or minus twenty percent, which is how nickel-metal-hydride packs achieve hundreds of thousands of cycles; cycling the same chemistry to full depth yields far fewer cycles, fewer even than lithium-ion.
claims.quote_verbatim: They go centered 50% point, plus or minus 20%. That's how you get hundreds of thousands of cycles out of nickel metal hydride.
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: The first generation of lithium cells was rated at roughly three hundred to four hundred cycles, energy-dense but not designed for longevity, because they were built for consumer products replaced every couple of years.
claims.quote_verbatim: they're only rated at about 300 to 400 cycles
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: DC fast charging bypasses the vehicle's onboard AC-DC stage and drives current straight into the pack; the handshake requests a current rather than a voltage, so the charger behaves as a current source and the pack voltage rises as it accepts the charge.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's putting out current right into your pack. No AC to then DC back to your DC pack inside your car.
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: Charging at high current drives cells to their upper voltage limit at a lower state of charge than trickling would, which is why a fast charge is terminated around eighty percent.
claims.quote_verbatim: when you have that kind of current going in, then you're pushing up to your maximum voltage earlier than you would if you were trickling it in, of course. And that's why you only go to the 80% point during a fast charge.
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: A battery management system measures every cell in the pack individually, and the single cell nearest its upper limit sets the pace for the whole pack; when that cell reaches its threshold the charge-current request is reduced and the cell can be shunted so the rest continue to fill.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's looking at all the cells. In fact, it's looking at every single one of them individually. And the one that is the closest to your top limit is the one that's setting the pace.
claims.speaker: Bob Simpson
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Bob Simpson - Ardent Automotive Artisan

claims.claim_text: A large aviation battery assembly consists of cells inside a steel enclosure together with the battery management and protection circuitry; in one recorded failure the assembly caught fire and melted internally despite that protection.
claims.quote_verbatim: all these battery cells in a huge battery management box, right? A big steel box with all the battery management and protection circuitry
claims.episode_title: Boeing, PCBs & Startups - Awful Airplane Aeration

claims.claim_text: A battery module can be specified without the ability to interrupt its own current when that function is assigned elsewhere in the system, which leaves the protection responsibility spanning a system boundary and is a candidate cause when a managed pack fails to shut itself down.
claims.quote_verbatim: apparently the battery wasn't able to shut off its own current. So, because that wasn't in the design spec for that battery module. The plane was supposed to have that elsewhere in the system.
claims.episode_title: Boeing, PCBs & Startups - Awful Airplane Aeration

claims.claim_text: Instrument runtime can be multiplied several times simply by choosing a cell format with more capacity: swapping a single nine-volt battery for four AA cells in a handheld meter turns a five-to-six-hundred-hour life into a two-to-three-thousand-hour one.
claims.quote_verbatim: I can take an existing multimeter that's got good battery life, like 500, 600 hours, and I can replace the 9-volt battery with four double A's
claims.episode_title: Boeing, PCBs & Startups - Awful Airplane Aeration

claims.claim_text: Powering a precision analogue circuit directly from cells lets the supply rail drift as the cells discharge, and any supply-dependent error term drifts with it; the fix is to insert a voltage regulator rather than run from the raw battery.
claims.quote_verbatim: the solution is to get a precise circuit is just whack a voltage regulator in, whereas I was just going to power it just from some batteries
claims.episode_title: Hamvention, Arduino and Intel - Burdensome Background Battology

claims.claim_text: A supply-voltage-dependent offset error can invert the usual test intuition: in one case the offset was worse at higher supply voltage, so the circuit measured badly on fresh cells and only came into specification as the cells approached end of life.
claims.quote_verbatim: the offset voltage is worse at a higher supply voltage. So when you put fresh batteries in, and that was the problem.
claims.episode_title: Hamvention, Arduino and Intel - Burdensome Background Battology

claims.claim_text: Cell internal resistance varies strongly with format: an AAA cell sits around 0.2 to 0.4 ohms while a nine-volt battery is on the order of an ohm, which limits deliverable current, causes the cell to heat under load, and makes the discharge self-limiting.
claims.quote_verbatim: a triple a battery is about 0.2 ohms or 0.2 to 0.4 ohms or something like that so a nine volt battery is you know it's probably an ohm
claims.episode_title: Hyperloop, Upverter and Soldering - Unbelievable USB Ustulater

claims.claim_text: The internal resistance quoted on a cell's data sheet is the ohmic term only and excludes ionic resistance, the contribution of the chemical reaction itself, which develops over timescales from a tenth of a second to tens of seconds and so is invisible in an instantaneous measurement.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's um ionic resistance in a battery and there's internal resistance and people think that they're one and the same
claims.episode_title: Hyperloop, Upverter and Soldering - Unbelievable USB Ustulater

claims.claim_text: A lithium-ion polymer pouch cell reaches about 4.2 volts fully charged and spends most of its discharge in a flat region near 3.7 volts; running a load from one cell therefore requires a boost converter, while stacking two cells in series raises the rail enough to remove that converter from the design.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a lithium ion polymer pouch cell. So the kind that's like 4.2 volt cutoff and then 3.7 roughly in the flat region
claims.episode_title: An Interview With Andrew Witte - Telistic Timepiece Technomania

claims.claim_text: A coulomb-counting fuel gauge integrates charge into and out of the pack rather than inferring state from terminal voltage, and combining that count with a model of the cell's discharge characteristic curve is what makes a percentage or bar-graph display meaningful.
claims.quote_verbatim: one of these charge gauge ICs that actually truly measures the charge going into the battery and then the charge coming out
claims.episode_title: Silego, ADCs & Seismic Detection - Dave's Dingo Dystocia

claims.claim_text: The presence of a voltage from an energy-harvesting source says nothing about available energy or power; arithmetic on the harvested power against a phone battery's capacity gives charging times measured in decades.
claims.quote_verbatim: people know that just because you have voltage doesn't mean you have energy or power in the case of when you're actually charging something

claims.claim_text: Ambient radio-frequency harvesting delivers so little average power that a receiver a metre from a Wi-Fi antenna would take weeks to fill a small cell; any apparently fast delivery afterwards comes from the battery's low impedance dumping stored energy, not from the harvester.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's just not going to capture enough energy to charge up, you know, it'd take like weeks and weeks to charge up the battery
claims.episode_title: Design Reviews Are Important - Habitual Hype Hebetude

claims.claim_text: Cells connected in series each need their own floating voltage measurement in the battery management system, plus a bypass path such as a shunt FET, because the pack terminal voltage alone cannot reveal an individual cell drifting out of range.
claims.quote_verbatim: If they're in series, yes. The battery management system will have a floating voltage measurement across each cell.
claims.episode_title: Last Minute Decisions - Obdurate Onepercenter Obstacles

claims.claim_text: Commercial off-the-shelf batteries flown in vacuum have to be stripped of PVC jacketing, because PVC outgasses chlorine and contaminates the surrounding spacecraft.
claims.quote_verbatim: for our batteries, for example, they have PVC jackets. So we have to cut out the PVC jackets
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Shaun Meehan - Doctiloquent Dove Deployer

claims.claim_text: A bench power supply is not an equivalent substitute for the battery it replaces during debugging, because a battery is a two-quadrant device that can sink current as well as source it, and a single-quadrant supply cannot absorb energy pushed back by the load.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not quite the same as a battery because a battery is a four, well, is a two quadrant device as well
claims.episode_title: Old Books, New Tricks - Iterant Inscription Irrationality

claims.claim_text: Any battery, including a primary cell not designed to be charged, will absorb current pushed back into it, for example from an inductive load whose current is interrupted, and charging a non-rechargeable cell hard enough makes it vent violently.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can charge batteries, even batteries that are not designed to be charged. You can sync current back into them.
claims.episode_title: Old Books, New Tricks - Iterant Inscription Irrationality

claims.claim_text: Charge rate is bounded by heat: the ceiling on how fast a phone-sized pack can be filled is a thermal limit in the cell, not a limitation of the charger electronics.
claims.quote_verbatim: You start to get limited by how fast your battery can even charge at that point. Yes. Yeah. Yeah. I know. It's a heat problem.
claims.episode_title: Compare and Contrast Tech Entitlement - Worldly Working Wonks

claims.claim_text: Alkaline has become the default primary chemistry for consumer cells and has displaced zinc-carbon on price; zinc-carbon cells remain purchasable but are rarely specified.
claims.quote_verbatim: alkaline is, you know, like, the standard one these days. Yeah. Like, nobody uses zinc-carbon anymore.
claims.episode_title: Consolidate All The Things - Zonked Zelotic Zaitech

claims.claim_text: In an electric drive the current ceiling is set on the battery side, not the motor side: a motor is essentially copper wire and will absorb as much power as it is given provided it is cooled, so the limit is the pack's safe discharge current and the capacity of the interconnects to carry it.
claims.quote_verbatim: the motor's just copper wire, right? It'll take as much... You know, as long as you cool the thing, it'll take as much power as you can dump in there

claims.claim_text: A single-cell lithium rail sits near 3.7 volts, which almost never matches the voltage a load needs, so a boost or DC-DC stage is the normal answer rather than stacking enough cells to reach a twenty-to-thirty-volt output and regulating down linearly.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can't put 20 to 30 volts worth of batteries in there and run everything linear

claims.claim_text: Replacing loose hobby-grade lithium-polymer cells with a packaged consumer USB power bank removes the custom charging circuit, the protection circuitry and the fuel-gauge telemetry from a one-off design at once, because those functions are already inside the purchased product and it can be re-bought off the shelf if damaged.
claims.quote_verbatim: instead of using freaking hobby, unregulated, you know, giant batteries that are meant to do, you know, seven, eight amps, draws or whatever, switching that out to one of those, like, little cell phone battery, you know, chargers

claims.claim_text: The energy cost of a high-level interpreted runtime is affordable on a mains-powered device and generally is not on a battery-powered one, which is why language choice on embedded targets tracks the power source.
claims.quote_verbatim: if they're battery powered then these kind of high-level languages are just not the right answer because of the amount of battery they take

claims.claim_text: A charge gauge reads the cell temperature alongside the charge count, which improves the state estimate; and a firmware change that stops a pack short of one hundred percent charge is the standard mitigation available when a cell-level defect cannot be fixed in the field.
claims.quote_verbatim: it actually takes physical readings too because it's reading the temperature of the battery as that's happening

claims.claim_text: Lithium charging parts have grown beyond simple chargers into management devices with control registers and state-of-charge reporting, so the same chip that regulates the charge also reports what level the pack is at.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's not just the charger anymore it's like the it's got other a bunch of other bells and whistles on it right so and it actually reports what level you're at

claims.claim_text: Smart packs that report their state over a management protocol are not interchangeable across suppliers: a substitute pack of the same nominal type failed to report voltage at all, which silently removed battery monitoring from a product built around the original pack's protocol.
claims.quote_verbatim: some batteries don't report voltage properly

claims.claim_text: Lithium-ion cells swell during charging and with age, and industry practice is to leave a defined mechanical clearance around a cell in the enclosure to accommodate that expansion; a rigid machined case removes that allowance.
claims.quote_verbatim: there are apparently, you know, some rules of thumb in the industry about how much slack around a lithium ion battery you have to leave

claims.claim_text: Pushing capacity by adding layers and thinning the separator leaves the cell less able to survive its own swelling: pressure from expansion punches through the thinned dielectric, shorts adjacent layers internally, and the resulting current is large enough that external protection circuitry cannot intervene.
claims.quote_verbatim: when it swells up due to the charging or use, it then puts pressure on those layers and punches through

claims.claim_text: An internal short inside a lithium cell is outside the reach of the pack's protection electronics, because the fault current circulates within the cell rather than through the protection path.
claims.quote_verbatim: The current is enormous and your external battery protection circuitry is not going to help you one bit.

claims.claim_text: Building electric-vehicle packs from 18650 cells lets a vehicle maker ride a cell market already scaled and paid down by laptop manufacturing, whereas a chemistry aimed only at grid storage has no comparable volume to amortise its development and manufacturing cost against.
claims.quote_verbatim: the Tesla car uses, and all their cars use the 18650 lithium ion cells. So they can leverage that market, that massive market.
claims.episode_title: Road trip to the deep space network

claims.claim_text: Home storage packs are commonly assembled at stack-up voltages around sixty volts, an order below the three-to-four-hundred-volt traction packs used in electric vehicles.
claims.quote_verbatim: They only did, like, 60-volt stack-ups.

claims.claim_text: The 18650 is the industry-standard cylindrical lithium cell and is the default choice for a design that does not need a custom form factor.
claims.quote_verbatim: 18650s because they're the industry standard

claims.claim_text: A product built at millions of units can fund the tooling for a battery in a custom form factor and amortise it across the run, while a lower-volume product is confined to catalogue cells; the cost of going custom is becoming the entire supply chain for that part, with no second source to fall back on.
claims.quote_verbatim: you alone can pay the tooling costs for a new kind of battery. That's got a special form factor because, you know, you've got the volumes necessary

claims.claim_text: In a modern smartphone the internal volume under the display is dominated by the cell: roughly sixty percent battery, about thirty percent circuit boards, and around ten percent camera modules on flex.
claims.quote_verbatim: what, 60% of it is battery?

claims.claim_text: Power budgeting can be entered from either end, and the two orders give different designs: fix the chipset and size the battery to the resulting consumption, or fix the battery size and select a chipset whose budget fits inside it.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can drive it from, I need to use this chip set. So therefore I need this size battery.

claims.claim_text: A gallon of gasoline carries on the order of thirty-two kilowatt-hours of energy, which is the reference figure against which battery energy density is judged.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's something like 32 kilowatt hours, the effective, you know, energy density, if you convert it to electricity.
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Jeff Keyzer - Comical Keyzer Comes a-Callin'

claims.claim_text: Progress in the battery chemistries actually in service has come from small incremental improvements to existing technology rather than from step changes, which is the basis for treating claimed breakthroughs from new entrants sceptically.
claims.quote_verbatim: Most of the progress in real battery technology, i.e. the stuff we're using today, has come from small incremental improvements in existing technology
claims.episode_title: Questioning Everyday Prototyping - Verrucose Vehicle Vitilitigation

claims.claim_text: An order-of-magnitude increase in battery energy density is not available within known chemistry; the growth achieved has been roughly linear, and claims of tenfold improvement, particularly manufacturable at scale, are inconsistent with that record.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's no way you're going to get an order of magnitude increase in energy density inside batteries

claims.claim_text: The term cell refers to the individual unit, such as a cylindrical 18650, while battery refers to the assembled article: multiple cells, a management unit of some kind, and the interconnects between them.
claims.quote_verbatim: I would refer to a battery as the assembled components, uh, which may include multiple cells and, and would include also a management unit of some kind and the connections between those individual cells

claims.claim_text: Mechanical simulation of a product containing a cell requires measuring the cell first: unlike a homogeneous metal, a battery has no tabulated stiffness or failure stress, so non-destructive stiffness tests are run on real cells and the measured values are back-calculated into the model.
claims.quote_verbatim: we want to measure the stiffness of the battery so that we can then use that information in simulation

claims.claim_text: Two cells built to the same published specification can differ in chemistry and reaction kinetics between manufacturers, so a mechanical failure threshold cannot be stated a priori for a battery the way it can for aluminium and has to be established by test.
claims.quote_verbatim: your chemistries are going to be different, um, potentially for different manufacturers, even with the same specifications

claims.claim_text: On a mobile robot the energy source is carried, and allocating around ten percent of vehicle mass to batteries is already generous; wanting two to eight hours of runtime on that allowance is the hard constraint on the design.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're a hundred pound robot, you maybe have 10 pounds for batteries, but that might be stretching it

claims.claim_text: At consumer volumes of tens of millions of units a year, a one-in-a-million battery failure rate is a serious problem rather than an acceptable defect level, which is why rare, hard-to-reproduce battery faults attract dedicated engineering effort at that scale.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you're building tens of millions of products a year and you have one in a million batteries explode, that that's a huge deal

claims.claim_text: Battery safety qualification is destructive and physical: test houses run nail-penetration machines that drive nails into cells to see whether they ignite, alongside crush tests such as driving a vehicle over the pack.
claims.quote_verbatim: the battery nail penetration testing machine is a machine that hammers nails into batteries to see if they explode

claims.claim_text: Lithium cells cannot be air-freighted as ordinary cargo, and overseas shipment is both expensive and restricted; some countries cannot be shipped to at all, and the carriers that will move cells charge heavily for it.
claims.quote_verbatim: You can't air ship them or stuff like that

claims.claim_text: Shipping restrictions rather than availability are what stop buyers in some countries getting lithium cells from the large distributors, and a distributor declining to ship to a destination is a regulatory signal rather than a stocking decision.
claims.quote_verbatim: I saw this on mouser. I can't get it cause they won't ship to my country. Can you ship it here?

claims.claim_text: Fitting a pack considerably larger than the load requires buys two things at once: a full day of untethered operation, and fewer charge cycles across the product's life because each cycle uses a smaller fraction of the pack.
claims.quote_verbatim: it has a 10-amp hour battery on it. Yeah. Which, at the time, I thought it was gratuitous
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Craig J Bishop

claims.claim_text: Integrated lithium charge controllers of the BQ2400x family provide roughly two amps of charge current when the system is idle and switch the system load automatically between the battery and the adapter, with control registers for configuration.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's a two-amp charger if the system's not running, but it switches the system load between the battery and the adapter automatically
claims.episode_title: An Interview with Craig J Bishop

claims.claim_text: An alkaline cell is effectively exhausted around 0.8 volts, where most of the energy has already been delivered, with about 99.99 percent gone by 0.5 volts.
claims.quote_verbatim: Normally 0.8. Is where most of it drops off. Although 0.5. Is technically. Where like 99.99% of the energy.

claims.claim_text: A cell that has fallen to its cutoff voltage under load will recover part of its charge once the load is removed, and how much comes back depends on how fast it was discharged, so a voltage reading taken under heavy load understates the remaining capacity.
claims.quote_verbatim: it depends on how fast you discharge them. As to how much charge you can actually recover.

claims.claim_text: The 18650 designation encodes the cell's dimensions: 18 millimetres in diameter by 65.0 millimetres long, the trailing zero being the decimal place on the length.
claims.quote_verbatim: The 18650 is 18 millimeters across by 65.0. That's what the extra zero.

claims.claim_text: A cylindrical lithium cell is a wound roll of electrode material about a metre long, so current from the innermost windings must travel that entire length to reach the tabs; the resulting internal series resistance limits the power the cell can deliver independently of its capacity.
claims.quote_verbatim: the current has to flow through that entire one meter roll if it wants to get out to those tabs. Right? So there's extra internal resistance.

claims.claim_text: Battery power should be avoided in a sensor fleet unless it is genuinely required: at a thousand nodes averaging three years of life, replacement becomes a continuous maintenance task, and the cells involved are expensive lithium primaries rather than cheap consumer cells.
claims.quote_verbatim: let's say you can get three years out of a thousand sensors on average. How often are you changing a battery?

claims.claim_text: Electric-vehicle DC fast charging follows a stepped curve rather than a constant rate: full power below fifty percent state of charge, a reduced step above it, and further reductions above sixty percent; every vehicle does this but the shape of the curve differs between models.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's actually a stepped charger. So like at below 50%, you'll get your full 50 kilowatts, but above 50, it'll drop down to 40 kilowatts.
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Cell-to-cell voltage deviation is used as an early indicator of an impending pack fault: one manufacturer's recall tightened the allowed spread to around 150 millivolts between the highest and lowest cell and shuts the vehicle down when it is exceeded.
claims.quote_verbatim: they've tightened up the maximum cell deviation. So that if, if it sees more than, I think it's 150 millivolts deviation between the highest and lowest cell, it will just shut the car down
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Pausing a charge at high state of charge, for instance at eighty and ninety percent, lets cell voltages settle so that the measured cell-to-cell deviation reflects the pack rather than transient charging offsets.
claims.quote_verbatim: they pause it, I think at 80 and 90% for a while. And I'm guessing again, that's probably just wait for it to stabilize and then check the cell deviation again.
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Eight-year pack warranties with a guaranteed remaining-capacity figure, written before any field history existed, are the commercial reason charge curves are derated: sustained high-power fast charging threatens the capacity the warranty promises.
claims.quote_verbatim: got to last eight years and it's got to have X capacity after eight years. And people are fast charging these things at 50 kilowatts. We'd better step it down
claims.episode_title: LEDs and EVs with Mike Harrison

claims.claim_text: Where the form factor permits it, enlarging the battery is a cheaper route to runtime than the last increments of firmware power optimisation, which yield diminishing savings for substantial added complexity.
claims.quote_verbatim: I just put a bigger battery on there. If you can do that, that's the easier solution.

claims.claim_text: A lithium-ion cell is charged to a termination voltage of 4.2 volts, and that voltage has to be held accurately, to roughly half a percent, because overshoot damages the cell.
claims.quote_verbatim: a lithium ion battery is charged at 4.2 volts. Right. And it's got to be pretty precise. Right. Yes. Right. It's got to be within like half a percent or something.

claims.claim_text: Charging a lithium-ion cell from a laboratory supply reproduces the standard algorithm directly: set the compliance voltage to 4.2 volts so it cannot be exceeded, run the supply in constant-current mode, and the supply transitions itself into constant-voltage float as the cell approaches full charge.
claims.quote_verbatim: you put the compliance voltage so it doesn't go over and you put it in a constant current mode

claims.claim_text: A defective charger or fixture can destroy successive replacement cells rather than one, and cells killed that way are generally unrecoverable; applying a fixed voltage for a set period to revive them does not reliably work.
claims.quote_verbatim: you can put a fixed voltage on them for a set period of time and try and, you know, try and revive the cells and stuff. But no, no, it just, just killed them dead.

claims.claim_text: Charging an electric-vehicle pack only to eighty or ninety percent as routine, reserving a full charge for trips that need the range, is a deliberate practice for extending pack life.
claims.quote_verbatim: I used to only charge mine to 80% unless I was like going on some big road trip

claims.claim_text: Power-tool battery packs expose four or five contacts: battery positive, battery negative, a coding or identification pin and a thermistor line; the tool uses only the thermistor and identification pins, while the additional contacts exist for the charger.
claims.quote_verbatim: So it's battery, battery plus, battery minus cod, which I guess is code. Um, and then there's a, the Mr. Um, pin as well.

claims.claim_text: Adapting an existing power-tool battery system as a general-purpose supply is attractive because the cells, the charger infrastructure and the retail availability already exist; the added interface is a printed or machined adapter with an inline fuse and switch.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's got like a fuse in line and a switch in line so that you can go and power your kids power wheels

claims.claim_text: A hybrid or storage inverter must speak the firmware protocol of the pack's management system, so it works only with one or a few battery brands; another brand may physically install but leaves the management non-functional.
claims.quote_verbatim: usually when you buy a hybrid inverter or any, or a battery storage inverter system, it usually only works with one or several brands of batteries

claims.claim_text: Accepting a subsidised or free inverter locks the installation to one battery manufacturer and often to specific models within that brand, so the apparent saving transfers into a constrained and possibly more expensive battery choice.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's only compatible with one specific brand of battery

claims.claim_text: Whether a load draws constant current or constant power decides how its consumption tracks the falling cell voltage: behind a linear regulator the current is fixed so input power falls as the battery drains, whereas behind a DC-DC converter the input power stays constant and the current rises.
claims.quote_verbatim: the DC to DC converter, constant power is going to be more accurate than your constant current, which will change with battery voltage as your battery voltage drops
claims.episode_title: At least my house isn't haunted

claims.claim_text: A general-purpose microcontroller is technically capable of implementing lithium charge control, but practitioners still buy a dedicated charge-management part because the consequences of a firmware error in that loop are severe.
claims.quote_verbatim: But this chip a hundred percent could be a battery charger charge control system. I'm just, I am personally a little bit too anxious to do it at this time.

claims.claim_text: When the battery is user-replaceable its negative terminal is no longer system ground, so a coulomb-counting shunt in that path has to be isolated; shorting across the shunt makes the device believe it is drawing no current at all, and using the same shunt for current control complicates charging a rechargeable cell.
claims.quote_verbatim: you accidentally short out your column counter on your device basically it believes it draws no current at all
claims.episode_title: Software Defined Power Supplies with Werner Johansson

claims.claim_text: An H-bridge on both sides of the transformer makes a battery interface bidirectional: power flows through it into the battery to charge, and back out through the transformer onto the high-voltage bus to discharge.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's basically got a H-bridge on both sides of the transformer so that it can feed power into the battery to charge the battery and then it can extract power from the battery

claims.claim_text: Rack-mounted home storage modules are heavy enough to dominate installation planning: each 19-inch battery module weighs around 41 kilograms and the empty rack itself around 91 kilograms, which can require a lift truck to unload.
claims.quote_verbatim: the batteries weigh like 41 kilos each, which isn't too bad, you know, but the actual rack itself weighs 91 kilos

claims.claim_text: A pre-wired battery rack turns capacity expansion into a mechanical operation: a spare slot takes another module, which is slid in and connected in minutes without rewiring the installation.
claims.quote_verbatim: there'll be spare slots in the rack. I just slot in a battery, plug it up, because the rack comes pre-wired

claims.claim_text: Spacecraft keep the batteries physically disconnected from the bus until deployment using separation switches that detect release from the dispenser, after which a timed sequence gates antenna deployment and then transmission.
claims.quote_verbatim: You have to have separation switches. So they detect when you're, when the doors opened, they'll be released. And that's what is holding the batteries disconnected from the rest of the bus
claims.speaker: Dan Esparon
claims.episode_title: Satellite Design Engineering with Dan Esparon

claims.claim_text: Splitting a spacecraft's storage into several smaller battery modules with their own management, rather than one large module, means the loss of one critical part costs a fraction of the energy system instead of all of it.
claims.quote_verbatim: if you have one big battery module or battery management system and you lose one critical part there, you lose your whole battery system or you can have five slightly larger battery systems and you've got that redundancy there
claims.speaker: Dan Esparon
claims.episode_title: Satellite Design Engineering with Dan Esparon

claims.claim_text: In a large electric vehicle the pack dominates the bill of materials, accounting for on the order of eighty percent of the cost.
claims.quote_verbatim: 80% of the cost is the battery

claims.claim_text: Alkaline cells leak more often than they once did across all brands, and the contributing factors are unsettled: temperature, humidity and pressure are implicated, and a stiff spring terminal pressing on the cell ends is a common hypothesis with no hard evidence behind it.
claims.quote_verbatim: everyone has their pet theory of why alkalines leak. And they leak more than what they used to.
claims.episode_title: Clap on, clap off, lights flicker

claims.claim_text: A twenty-five kilowatt-hour domestic pack can be fully discharged in a single day once dryer, oven, cooktop and an unplanned electric-vehicle charge are on it, while a frugal evening of lighting, refrigeration and a little cooking consumes only twenty to twenty-five percent of it.
claims.quote_verbatim: i could use the entire 25 kilowatt hour battery in a day

claims.claim_text: A pack can report itself as charging while actually discharging: in one laptop the system indicated charge in progress and the charger's own indicator lit, yet the pack fell overnight, then charged to fifty percent and stopped, with the fault reproduced across two different chargers so the charger was eliminated as the cause.
claims.quote_verbatim: Windows indicated that it was charging. And the charging LED on the side of the little magnetic plug-in, you know, charger doodad. It all lit up. Windows lit up and said it's charging. But it didn't charge.

claims.claim_text: A used pack legitimately reports reduced full-charge capacity against its original rating, but it should still charge to one hundred percent of that reduced capacity; failure to reach the indicated full state is a distinct fault from ordinary capacity fade.
claims.quote_verbatim: it's lost some of its capacity. But batteries should still charge to 100%, correct? Right? They should still indicate 100%.

claims.claim_text: A storage battery module can be taken out of service by its management firmware rather than by its cells: one rack module had to be shut down while the cells themselves remained healthy, the defect being early firmware in the module's controller.
claims.quote_verbatim: Batteries, the cells are still healthy, whatever. It's just the... Cells are healthy. The computer. The computer's got problems.

claims.claim_text: Battery chemistry has improved by evolution rather than by radical steps, so a design guide can treat the available chemistries as a stable menu while noting that the numbers move steadily; the larger change for product designers has been the shrinking of cells into very small form factors, which shifts the burden onto designs that sip current and wake only briefly.
claims.quote_verbatim: It's getting progressively better, but it's a slow progression. There haven't been any radical breakthroughs.
claims.episode_title: Applied Embedded Electronics with Jerry Twomey

claims.claim_text: Cells tested against the figures printed on their own data sheet have been found to melt internally, which is an argument for verifying cell performance by measurement rather than accepting the published specification.
claims.quote_verbatim: he did a battery testing them to their specifications. That was on their data sheet and it failed. They like melted inside.

claims.claim_text: Early portable calculators used vacuum fluorescent displays, whose heated element wasted power even though it lowered the voltage requirement, and the resulting consumption forced the use of bulky C or D cells.
claims.quote_verbatim: the first portable display technology were VFDs and they were still problematic because they, they used a heated element. So they, they actually waste power
claims.episode_title: The Secret Life of Circuits with lcamtuf / Michał Zalewski

claims.claim_text: The word battery came into electrical use by analogy with a battery of cannon, applied to any powerful arrangement; when Volta published his description of the first electric battery in 1800 he called it an artificial electric organ, a name that did not survive.
claims.quote_verbatim: when Volta published his description of his battery in 1800, the first electric battery, he didn't call it a battery. He called it an artificial electric organ.
claims.episode_title: The Lightning Tamers with Kathy Joseph

claims.claim_text: Moving the cells off a head-mounted display into a belt-worn puck connected by a thin cable kept the headset light while carrying about six hours of battery.
claims.quote_verbatim: It had this little puck thing that you could clip on your belt and it had a little thin wire that ran up to the headset. And inside the puck was like six hours worth of batteries
claims.speaker: Jeri Ellsworth
claims.episode_title: Jeri Ellsworth and the demise of CastAR

claims.claim_text: A battery subsystem is more than the cell: the design also has to answer how the pack is charged and how the user is told the charge is running low.
claims.quote_verbatim: there's not just the battery, there's the, how do you charge it? And how do you tell people their batteries going low?

claims.claim_text: Monitoring pack voltage and shedding the load when it falls below a threshold is the basic protection against over-discharge in an unattended solar installation, and is implemented in the controller of solar lighting towers and repeater sites.
claims.quote_verbatim: i've used it to control a few lighting towers to um manage battery voltages and just cut lights out if the voltage is too low

claims.claim_text: A multi-cell pack whose terminal voltage sits near that of a single cell is wired in parallel rather than in series, so pack voltage is a direct read on the series count.
claims.quote_verbatim: It was showing three and a half volts, so it wasn't fully charged, so they must have been all in parallel
claims.episode_title: Road trip to the deep space network

claims.claim_text: Sealed remote sensor units carrying their own cells are commonly specified for a five-year service life with no intervention, which makes average power consumption, not sensing performance, the governing design constraint.
claims.quote_verbatim: you have these pucks, and they have their own batteries, and they have to last for five years
claims.episode_title: Greg Charvat Returns With A Book! - Laboratory Literature Laureate

claims.claim_text: A battery-powered camera cannot sustain continuous operation, so wireless camera products are built around periodic removal and recharging on a magnetic mount rather than a permanent installation.
claims.quote_verbatim: you pull these things off their mounts and you go plug them in and then you charge them up and they come back out
